annotations.text:
Vault explorer — three directions for the same vault.

All three show the real tree on this machine: workspaces, project nodes, _bot.md beside a node, and .devdeck with its features. Indigo means vault (committed, travels with the repo); green means personal (never leaves this machine).

Each artboard has a dark/light switch above it.

Recommendation: A.

It is the only one that answers all three of your asks in one surface — the whole vault, one node in detail, and a place for bots and agents to live — without a second screen.
B trades the inspector for depth: you see more of the tree at once, and file meaning rides along each row. Best if you mostly want to find a file.
C never makes you scroll a deep tree — each level is a column and the path is always visible. Costs the most horizontal room, and it is unfamiliar in a dev tool.

Pick a folder and the right side summarises it; pick a file and it becomes the file. Same layout, two states — no third pane.

Read-only by default, because a bot writes most of these. Edit is a deliberate act, not a cursor landing in a file the DevDeck bot rewrites at 08:00.
